title: Voting Awareness Campaign
content:
Conducted a large-scale awareness drive encouraging Beary youth and families to become responsible citizens by casting their votes.

Arranged 30+ free buses to Dakshina Kannada during the MP Elections to facilitate voting for community members working in Bengaluru.

Engaged with private-sector employers to request election-day leave for employees, ensuring no one misses their democratic right.

Met the State Election Commissioner to formally request mandatory leave for private-sector employees on election day.

title: 🌙 Eid Summit & Iftar Meet
content:
BCC proudly organizes annual Eid Summit and Iftar Meet programs that bring together hundreds of Beary community members in Bengaluru for meaningful celebrations. These distinguished gatherings serve as platforms for unity, cultural connection, and strengthening bonds across generations.

Highlights:

  • Community-wide Iftar gatherings promoting brotherhood and unity
  • Recognition and felicitation of Beary achievers from various fields
  • Networking opportunities for professionals, students, and families
  • Cultural programs celebrating our rich Islamic and Beary heritage

title: MEMBERSHIP CAMPAIGN
content:
Uniting Bengaluru’s Beary Community Under One Platform

BCC launched a groundbreaking membership campaign that witnessed an overwhelming response from the community. Thousands of Bearys participated on the very first day, demonstrating the strong desire for unity and collective representation. The campaign successfully mobilized Bearys across Bengaluru to join the Bearys Central Committee, creating a powerful network of support, advocacy, and cultural preservation.

Campaign Highlights:

  • Thousands enrolled on day one, showcasing massive community support
  • Door-to-door outreach across all Bengaluru localities
  • Community meetings and awareness sessions in multiple zones
  • Simplified registration process ensuring easy participation for all

title: BEARYS – THE GUARDIAN OF COAST
content:
“History remembers the bravery of the Beary sailors who served under Rani Abbakka Chowta of Ullal. When the Portuguese tried to seize the Mangalore port in the 16th century, the local Muslim mariners formed the vanguard of the resistance. Their knowledge of the tides and their fearless naval tactics kept the invaders at bay for decades.”

Haider Ali, the ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore, established a navy based in Mangalore for the first time around 1763. After capturing the coastal city of Bednore (and its subordinate port, Mangalore) in 1763, Haider Ali used it to build a naval fleet to counter European powers, specifically the British and Portuguese. The first fleet consisted of roughly 10 large ships (dhows) and 30 smaller vessels (ketches). The navy was created to protect trade, prevent piracy, and combat the British East India Company. Due to losses in skirmishes, Haider Ali began rebuilding a stronger navy in 1778, employing Dutch and European advisors to build ships at Bhatkal and Mangalore. Although his son, Tipu Sultan, is more famously recognized for expanding the navy and establishing a Board of Admiralty, Haider Ali is credited with making the initial effort to establish a dedicated naval force in Mangalore in the early 1760s.

title: The Brave Hearts (Beary Warriors and Freedom Fighters)
content:
Kutty Pokar Markar (16th Century):

• Role: Naval General.

• Contribution: A legendary admiral from the house of the Marakkars (Zamorin’s navy) who fought alongside Rani Abbakka Chowta of Ullal. He successfully destroyed the Portuguese fort in Mangalore in 1570, symbolizing the early local resistance against European colonialism.

Mohammad Nasrullah Manna (1918–2008):

• Role: Freedom Fighter (“Manna Saheb”).

• Contribution: A Gandhian leader from Thokur near Mangalore. He was a prominent figure in the Quit India Movement (1942) and was imprisoned for nine months by the British. He remained a respected community leader and traditional healer after independence.

The Unknown Sailors of Rani Abbakka:

• Role: The Mapilla/Beary Navy.

• Contribution: You can create a panel dedicated to the collective bravery of the local Muslim sailors who formed the backbone of Ullal’s defense. When Abbakka’s palace was attacked, she reportedly took refuge in a mosque, and her Muslim soldiers launched a midnight counter-attack to reclaim the city.

title: The Visionaries (Education & Social Reform)
content:
C. Mahmood (1874–1954):

• Role: Pioneer of Modern Education.

• Contribution: Despite being formally illiterate himself, he recognized that the community’s future lay in secular education. He founded the Badria Educational Institution in 1924 in the Bunder area. It was the first institution in the region to offer modern schooling alongside religious values, changing the destiny of thousands of Beary families.

Haji M. Kunhamu & Haji M. Moidinabba:

• Role: Philanthropists and Co-founders.

• Contribution: Key associates of C. Mahmood who helped establish the Muslim Educational Association (1927). They worked to create a network of support for students from poor economic backgrounds.

title: The Litterateurs Llanguage & Culture)
content:
B. M. Idinabba (1920–2009):

• Role: Poet, Politician, and “Kannada Kattaalu” (Protector of Kannada).

• Contribution: Perhaps the most iconic modern figure. A three-time MLA from Ullal, he was a bridge between the Beary and Kannada identities. He was the first President of the Beary Sahithya Sammelana (Beary Literature Summit) and famously wore a white khadi suit and Gandhi cap, embodying the nationalist spirit.

Ahmed Noori:

• Role: Scholar and Historian.

• Contribution: Author of “Maikala,” a seminal book on the history of Mangalore and its Muslim community. His work is the primary source for much of the oral history and heritage of the region.
